items.body: Review by TheEliteExtremophile — I've found Elder's work to be a bit inconsistent over their last few releases. After the stellarLore and Reflections of a Floating World, Omens was spotty and failed to deliver on the band'spromise of change. The Gold and Silver Sessions were an interesting (if unnecessary) foray intokrautrock. ELDOVAR was a neat collaboration album; and while I liked Innate Passage, it's not arecord I've found myself returning to. Last year's EP was also a bit of a split decision from me,with one good-but-not-exactly-memorable song and one fantastic one.Across the span of these last few releases, I've sensed that Elder has had a desire to more fullyembrace progressive rock, but they've had a hard time escaping some of the songwriting tricks andpatterns they've long utilized.Through Zero, Elder's seventh (or eighth or ninth, depending on how one counts splits/collaborations) full-length album, is their greatest success since 2017's Reflections. On thisrecord, they've fully embraced progressive rock while also maintaining their unique voice.Synthesizers and other keyboards are integrated more fully here than anywhere else in theirdiscography. Their classic heavy psych stylings are still prominent and an integral part of theirmusic, but they're supported by a greater diversity of sounds. Literal textures and tones, as wellas melodies and songwriting styles, are more varied on this record than they've been before.The album begins with "Sigil to Ruin". As the song slowly fades in, the lead guitar line makesallusions to the Canterbury sound, immediately making this unique within Elder's body of work. It'sstill firmly rooted in their heavy psych/post-rock tendencies, but it's nice to hear them genuinelyexpand their palette of influences. The opening verse is understated, but the guitar partsunderpinning it are complex and jazzy. In the song's second half, things get a bit heavier but stillsomewhat restrained by Elder's standards.The final stretch of the song sees synthesizers come to the front of things, channeling earlykrautrock and space rock like on last year's "Dream State Return". Elder has dabbled in krautrockbefore, but this is their most successful and distinctive venture into it. It's not until the finalminute of the song that the band fully unloads with their usual heaviness, and keeping it until theclimax like that helps this stand out when compared to other works they've done."Capture/Release" has another quiet introduction, this time with some more electronic touches. Whenthe guitar comes in, it's rather jangly and light, reminding me of certain math rock bands I'veheard. It doesn't take long for Elder to crank things up, though, with distorted guitars andsynthesizers harmonizing in a unique way. Guitars and keys come in alternating heavy and lightwaves, encapsulating this song's contrasting title well.Up next is the album's title track. Heavily flanged guitar leads the way on the most obviouscallback to Elder's stoner metal roots yet. But those stoner roots are combined with progressiverock's technicality and uncommon rhythms. The opening verse is rather mellow in comparison, withbroad, echoing clean guitar lines. Elder smoothly transitions to heavier, more intense riffs,supported by some synth lines that channel acts like Camel and Yes more than Tangerine Dream orearly Kraftwerk. The song's closing passage is classic Elder, with majestic soloing and triumphalchord progressions.The opening of "Strata" sees Elder going full post-rock, with a ringing, atmospheric bassline andairy, abstract guitar passages. This composition features another excellent and naturalistic build-up in intensity. Riffs are complex and powerful, with a strong sense of upward momentum. I love thetextures that the band constructs in this song. Layers of heavily-affected guitar lines andsynthesizers overlap, morph, swell, and bloom beautifully. Near the end, there's even a dash ofacoustic guitar which lends some beautiful contrast."Sight Unseen" provides a much-appreciated bit of respite in its opening. Airy keyboard and guitarlines float dreamily, and a calm but steady drum pattern provides some direction. Cosmic synthesizerarpeggios eventually come to the lead as fuzzy guitar licks add some nice grit. The drumming becomesmore insistent, and the bass subtly growths beneath the synths before the band explodes into heavypsychedelic majesty.The album ends on "Blighted Age". It's another mellow moment on the album, with acoustic guitar,electric piano, and mild electronic embellishments supporting some downcast-sounding vocals. Aftersuch a powerful, intense record, this is an occasion where ending on a mellower moment works reallywell.Through Zero is Elder's best release in at least nine years, if not ever. The sound presented hereis still unmistakably them, but it demonstrates a real evolution in their sound. Keyboards add a lotof depth and variance to the sound, and the songwriting is both fresh and original.Originally published here: theeliteextremophile.com/2026/06/22/album-review-elder-through-zero/

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑标志着乐队在融合风格上的成熟：他们在保留迷幻摇滚与后摇滚根基的同时，大幅扩展了合成器与键盘的应用，引入了Canterbury场景的爵士化吉他编排与德国Krautrock的太空感音色。开篇曲从清新的吉他引子缓慢展开，合成器在歌曲后半段才逐步涌向前台，重量级失真吉他被刻意留至终曲高潮，使情绪张力在节奏上拉开层次。后续曲目在电子化氛围与重型段落之间交替推进，标题曲则以法兰吉效果吉他向乐队早期石器摇滚致敬，呈现出对自身风格谱系的回顾意识。对于喜爱前卫摇滚框架内融合元素杂糅的听众而言，这是一张在边界拓展上较为克制的作品。

items.body: Review by TheEliteExtremophile — Apparently Tusm�rke put out an album last year that I missed, but they're prolific enough, there'snever that long a gap without them on this site. Balderdom (Baldness) follows in a template similarto Dawn of Oberon, in that it consists of a handful of shorter songs and a side-long epic.Tusm�rke's unique Norse-folk-prog is on proud display here, and this is another strong entry intheir catalog."Svensk dr�m" ("Swedish Dream") starts off with a fittingly dreamy atmosphere. Chimes, Mellotron,flute, and wordless vocals weave together. Nordic folk melodies lend this piece a light bounciness,but there are bassy blasts of either brass or synth that counterbalance that, lending some weight toan otherwise-floating (albeit somewhat eerie) composition.In contrast to the sylvan tones of the opener, "Balderdom (Tres Jolie)" is a peppy bit ofpsychedelic pop that draws from space-jazz. There's a bright joyousness to this piece, and theeffects on the vocals remind me of certain late '60s acts, like The Small Faces. This song's secondhalf is sparer and more atmospheric, and the band's folky influences crop up more prominently."Return of Forever (Stravinsky)" features some weird and wonky keyboard lines. Classical, folk, andjazz elements mingle, with a choir playing a prominent role alongside glittering synths and crunchyelectric piano.Closing out side A, "Vi er et kollektiv" ("We Are a Collective") has some twangy, folky guitar. Thatguitar cuts through the murky and swirling backdrop of piano, bass, wordless vocals and tight, jazzydrumming. The rhythm here is insistent, like some kind of crazy march. The group vocals helpunderscore the title, and the second half features a great, Canterbury-inspired organ solo.Side B is consumed by the 21-minute epic "Lidskjalv". (Google translate tells me that apparentlythis translates to "scott_scott" in Norwegian. Great job, Google. But in the related Icelandiclanguage, it means "Tremor", so I'm guessing it means something similar here.)Jazz elements are immediately at the forefront, with jangly guitar and shiny synths leading the way.Classic prog influences abound, as well, with Wakemanesque synth lines adding some propulsiveness.Recorder complements the synth quite well, both having a wonderful brightness to them.As this piece progresses, it freely moves between Norse folk and classic Anglo-prog as its basis.While the transitions between these moments can occasionally be jarring, the individual elements arestrong, and the moments where the two musical traditions truly meld are stellar. Each individualinstrumental element is beautiful and complex, and they fit together without stepping on any toes.Despite that, the instrumental midsection of this song does run a smidge long.The "Heimdal" section of this opus is fun and dramatic, balancing classic prog's over-the-toppretension and theatricality with Tusm�rke's unique playfulness. Odd-time and anxious patterns are agreat contrast to brighter moments in this song.Balderdom is another excellent outing from Tusm�rke. Their signature blend of styles is as strong asever, and this record demonstrates a great deal of creativity and flexibility. The closing opus doeshave a bit of bloat to it, but beyond that, there's not much to critique here.Originally published here: theeliteextremophile.com/2026/05/18/album-review-tusmorke-balderdom/

items._cn_summary: 挪威乐队Tusmørke延续其北欧民谣与前卫摇滚融合的风格，推出专辑《Balderdom》。专辑A面由四首较短曲目组成，开篇以钟琴、键盘、长笛与人声营造梦幻氛围，随后融入太空爵士元素与迷幻流行色彩，Canterbury风格的管风琴独奏亦点缀其中。B面为长达21分钟的史诗曲《Lidskjalv》，融合北欧民谣、盎格鲁前卫摇滚、爵士与古典成分，键盘线条受Wakeman影响，录音机与合成器交织形成明亮质感。乐队在北欧传统与英式前卫之间自由切换，部分过渡虽稍显突兀，但两种传统真正融合的时刻颇为出色。评论者对乐器编排的丰富性与整体水准给予肯定，但指出器乐中段略长。

items.body: Review by TheEliteExtremophile — I will be totally honest. Neurosis is one of those bands that I know has been massively influentialbut which I'm simply not that familiar with. I've listened to Through Silver in Blood, and that is afantastic record. I also know they're considered one of the primary progenitors of post-metal as adistinct genre, along with Isis, whose former vocalist and bassist has joined the band. (I have runacross folks trying to insist that post-metal and atmospheric sludge metal (another term frequentlyused to describe Neurosis's work) as being distinct. There may be a technical argument to be madethere, insofar as there is non-sludgy post-metal, but I don't think there's any atmospheric sludgeI've heard I couldn't also describe as post-metal.) That is to say, I went into this record blind.An Undying Love for a Burning World is Neurosis's 13th full-length release and their first in adecade. I'd heard it getting some positive buzz, so I decided to give it a spin. And boy, am I happyI did!After a brief, anguished spoken-word intro, "Mirror Deep" bursts forth with an awkward, stompingriff and oppressive buzzsaw synthesizers adding to the suffocating mood. This is quickly supplantedby a more Floydian scene. The synths smooth out, and guitar wavers beautifully across this sparebacking. This song whipsaws between these extremes effortlessly. Rather than being jarring, thesecontrasts only enhance the power of this song.In contrast to the prior song's explosive opening, "Fist Red Rays" flutters open with synthesizersand a more deliberate guitar passage. Things are more meditative and contemplative here, withrepetition playing a major role. There are stuttering, sludgy riffs aplenty during the verses. Theinstrumental midsection again dips into obvious Pink Floyd allusions, but it manages to soundincredibly fresh."Blind" strikes a sound somewhere between the first two pieces. It lays the synths on fairly thickat moments, keeping the visceral power of the guitars at the forefront all the while. Neurosis showsan impressive knack for knowing when to dial back the intensity and let the space breathe for amoment. The pairing of clean and harsh vocals during an extended atmospheric section is striking andpowerful, and the climax of this piece is especially crushing."Seething and Scattered" is fittingly angry, with some of the most direct riffs on the whole record.They've dialed down the "atmospheric" element of their sludge metal here, but it's still enthrallingand complex. Riffs are anxious and unsettled, slashing and crashing all about, until it suddenlygives way to a passage that is austere but beautiful. Dashes of krautrock are evident in the syntharrangement. Guitars gradually build back up, swelling in intensity, but they maintain a lush, fluidcharacter, like a roiling river.The shortest proper song on An Undying Love is "Untethered", at just over four minutes. Strains ofpsychedelia and some jazzy flourishes (especially in the keys) give this a unique feel when comparedto most of the rest of the record, and its relative directness is a nice change of pace.An Undying Love ends on a pair of ten-plus minute epics, the first of which is "In the WaitingHours". Its opening moments are quiet and stripped-back, but when the full band comes in, the riffsare thick and oppressive. Here, Neurosis really leans into the atmospheric side of atmosphericsludge. The riffs swell and dissolve into one another conveying the emotional weight of the music inabstract waves. The maelstrom does eventually abate in the final few minutes, providing the band onefinal, powerful build-up.Closing things out is the 17-minute "Last Light". Icy, eerie electronics kick this piece off,immediately lending it a unique character. Even after guitars join in, the synths continue to hissand sizzle. There's a sense of lurching, unstoppable momentum to this epic.�Neurosis plays around with some hopeful, major-key sounds at moments on this song, which is a starkdifference to elsewhere on this album. Giving the final track on such a huge album that kind ofupward lift was a brilliant move. It feels marvelously cathartic after all the musical rage thatpreceded this.The second half of this song features some gothic and post-punk touches. This ability to write suchinternally-diverse songs while also maintaining a sense of coherence truly demonstrates why Neurosisis such a marquee act in the metal world.Neurosis's return to recording is an impressive musical statement. The band skillfully blends therich, abstract textures of post-metal with the punishing intensity of sludge. The sprawlingcompositions on this album demonstrate intelligent and creative songwriting, with multiplesubsections within each piece locking together perfectly.Originally published here: theeliteextremophile.com/2026/05/11/album-review-neurosis-an-undying-love-for-a-burning-world/
items._cn_summary: 这是Neurosis乐队时隔十年发行的第十三张全长专辑，延续其标志性的后金属与泥浆金属底色，并在氛围营造上大量引入合成器元素。文章详细分析了开场曲在沉重riff与Pink Floyd式空灵段落之间的剧烈切换，后续曲目在冥想氛围、脏脏吉他riff与迷幻合成器之间交替推进。乐评特别提到乐队对张力收放的掌控——知道何时减弱强度让空间呼吸，以及清声与嘶吼人声并置所产生的冲击。Krautrock合成器编排、爵士化点缀和迷幻元素被多次提及，显示出明显的跨风格融合意图。整体而言，这是一张在厚重riff结构中嵌入氛围合成器与迷幻元素的实验性后金属作品，适合对氛围/实验跨界融合感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by TheEliteExtremophile — I briefly touched on Gong's convoluted history and past output in my review of their last album,2023's Unending Ascending, so I will not go into it in depth here. But this lineup?long bereft ofany original members but operating under the blessing of the band's late founder?has just put outits fourth full full-length release, Bright Spirit. In general, this album largely stays in linewith this incarnation of Gong's modus operandi. It's fun and lighthearted prog with heavypsychedelic infusions.Indic instrumentation kicks the album off on the 10-minute "Dream of Mine", and that easternaesthetic is retained once the band joins in. Guitar and sax twist atop a hypnotic rhythm, and theverses are hazy and exotic. As the song enters its midsection, group vocals and an ascendantinstrumental backing imbue this piece with a sense of soaring optimism. I love the way the bandcontinually brings back the opening theme; it really helps tie this piece together. The closingpassage, in particular, is classic Gong, as they meditate upon that main riff, allowing lush synthpads to swirl around it."Mantivule" is more anxious and jumpier in its opening, with speedy palm-muted guitar lines slinkingabout. The saxophone lines are a bit more easygoing, lending some nice internal variety. Somesurprisingly metallic riffage emerges near the middle of this song, and coupled with the jazzypercussion that follows, a comparison to "Larks' Tongues in Aspic" is warranted.Rich, gently-warbling synthesizers provide a warm intro to "The Wonderment". This song is unhurried,but it doesn't feel dragged out. The soothing atmosphere and deliberate pace add to the sense of,well, wonderment. "Stars in Heaven" draws heavily from '90s alt-rock, giving Gong's usual astralexplorations a more-grounded feel. Guitars and sax still float upward, but they attain just minorlevitation, as opposed to their usual full-force take-off."Fragrance of Paradise" dips into late '60s psychedelia in its opening moments, with an Indic-tingedbit of folk rock. Much like incense smoke, the music here drifts slowly and lazily upward, bringingwith it a sense of obscure mysticism. Gradually, the music solidifies. Wiry and energeticinstrumental lines weave together beneath deliberately-sung verses. The final minutes of this songup the intensity even more, bringing some rather heavy riffs (by Gong standards, at least).Things slow back down on "Relish the Possibility". It's not my favorite song here, but it's not bad.The textures and overall atmosphere are nice, but it doesn't do a ton to grab my attention.The album ends with "Eternal Hand". Some lyrical motifs reemerge here that were featured earlier inthe record, and the mood of the music is slightly haunting but with a glimmer of hope. Flute andjazzy clean guitar interlock to cultivate a delicate and shimmering composition.Bright Spirit is another solid addition to this current chapter of Gong's history. Gong isn't tryingto reinvent the wheel. Their brand of smooth and spacey psychedelic prog works well. This isprobably my least-favorite of this lineup's four albums, to be entirely honest, but that's not for alack of good material. The other three records, for me at least, simply had higher highs. While justabout everything here is really solid, there aren't any killer, knock-out songs.Originally published here: theeliteextremophile.com/2026/04/20/album-review-gong-bright-spirit/
items._genre: Canterbury Scene / psychedelic prog / jazz-rock fusion
items._cn_summary: Gong的《Bright Spirit》是当前乐队阵容的第四张全长专辑，延续了轻松愉悦的前卫摇滚路线，融入大量迷幻元素。印度风格乐器开篇，吉他与萨克斯在催眠式节奏上交织，旋律朦胧异域；中段合唱与器乐攀升带来乐观情绪，主题反复回归将全曲紧密串联。《Mantivule》节奏焦躁跳跃，金属化 riff 与爵士打击乐并存，接近 King Crimson 式的张力。《The Wonderment》合成器温暖，氛围舒缓悠远；《Stars in Heaven》借鉴九十年代另类摇滚，使星际探索更接地气。《Fragrance of Paradise》从六十年代末迷幻汲取灵感，民俗摇滚与神秘主义氛围交织，尾声加重 riff 提升强度。《Eternal Hand》以长笛与爵士清音吉他交织出微光闪烁的收束。整体而言，这是一张扎实但未试图重塑自身风格的作品。

items.body: Review by TheEliteExtremophile — I don't know what keeps drawing progressive and technical thrash metal bands to outer space, but itseems to be working. Vektor, Droid, Voivod, Obliveon, and plenty of others have plumbed the depthsof the night sky for inspiration, and Cryptic Shift continues in this proud tradition. Their 2020debut, Visitations from Enceladus, is a phenomenal work, with the 25-minute "Moonbelt Immolator"being one of the greatest metal epics of this century.Their newest release, Overspace & Supertime, is a monumental work, clocking in at nearly 80 minutesover just five songs. Their brand of cosmic, death-tinged thrash is a powerful canvas for their sci-fi storytelling."Crygenically Frozen" opens with unsettling clean guitar licks and obvious jazzy overtones. The moodis disorienting and claustrophobic, and the expositional narration is unobtrusive. When the songfinally gets going, the riffs interpolate between thrashy palm-muted passages and broader moments ofclean tones. The band does an excellent job at balancing some of their jazzy inclinations amidstextended passages of biting, metallic fury.The nearly-30-minute "Stratocumulus Evergaol" follows, again leading with askew-sounding cleanguitar, swirling about in a confusing fog. Everything is murky and indistinct in this openingpassage, effectively evoking the titular clouds. The harshness increases gradually, swelling andebbing over the first few minutes. There are some interesting ideas and textures here, but after awhile, it does feel like they're belaboring things a bit.When Cryptic Shift finally kicks things into high gear, it's exhilarating. The riffs are adrenaline-pumping and dazzlingly complex, and I love all the subtle flourishes the bassist gets in beneath itall. The different sub-sections of this opus flow together smoothly. Different riffs morph andevolve, sometimes abruptly and sometimes smoothly, but it always feels intentional. There's a cleardramatic arc to this work, with moments of smothering chaos as well as wide-open adventure.The band also knows when to give the listener some breathing room, sprinkling in occasional cleanbreaks. This contrast is essential to keeping the song flowing. And as much as I like this piece,I'm not really sure structuring it as one 30-minute piece makes the most sense. There were a fewnatural lulls where splitting this piece may have made the record a bit more wieldy."Hyperspace Topography" gets right into things, with energetic riffs bursting forth. Chords andscales are unusual, and jazz-tinted adornments add a lot of depth. The band dives into somewonderfully crazy instrumental experiments in the midsection of this song. Guitars squeal andskitter and roar, and the rhythm is constantly unsettled and unpredictable. Rhythmic weirdnesscontinues on "Hexagonal Eyes (Diverity Trepaphymphasyzm)", and I again really appreciate their moreunusual instrumental experiments. This song's second half sees Cryptic Shift play around a lot withclean guitar tones and some stripped-back atmospheres.I just glossed over two songs and 20 minutes of music in relatively few words, and that highlights arecurring pattern on this record for me. There is a lot of music here, and it is mostly very good,but I find it oddly tough to write about. There are only so many ways to say "there are a lot ofcool, technical riffs, and everything fits together really well."Overspace & Supertime closes on its 20-minute title track. Cryptic Shift channels Cynic in theopening passage, with vast-sounding, echoing clean guitar lines and ample jazz touches. When themetal returns, the riffs are crazy and inventive, and the band's bassist puts on an especiallystrong show. After the first verse, there are some spooky, theremin-like synth tones that gel wellwith this band's sci-fi themes.As elsewhere on this album, the band also knows when to break things up. Moments of abstractdistortion and noise occasionally crop up, and moments of gentleness and more overt sci-fi tonesalso help to keep things interesting. Near the middle of this epic, there is an extended passagewhere things become quite ethereal, and I really enjoyed hearing the band be more restrained. Thisepic's final movement is filled with as much gravity as one would expect. Jittery riffs wriggletheir way up and down the guitarists' fretboards. Unusual chords ring out and add a sense of majestyand grandiosity.Cryptic Shift's new record is a massive, ambitious work, and it is mostly a resounding success. Itis very rare for a record with an average song length north of 15 minutes to not have some bloat orexcess, but everything here is structured wonderfully. The band also has a good sense for when itwould be prudent to add some sonic contrasts, especially in a genre as tonally-limited as thrashmetal often can be.Originally published here: theeliteextremophile.com/2026/03/09/album-review-cryptic-shift-overspace-supertime/

items.body: The Joy Thieves, the Chicago industrial collective, released “I’ll Be Your Hammer” on 7 July 2026, a single and video featuring Chris Connelly. The track is taken from the album “Apocalypse Pending”, out now on the London label Armalyte Industries. Inside ‘I’ll Be Your Hammer’ The song reworks the title of The Velvet Underground’s “I’ll Be Your Mirror” into a line of resistance. Connelly sets the two against each other: “‘I’ll Be Your Mirror’ by The Velvet Underground is an introspective plea from one lover to another; ‘I’ll Be Your Hammer’ is written from the perspective of an individual standing up to a fascist regime. The more you suppress our rights, the stronger I get.” The video was directed by Joel Lopez of Lumbra Productions. Dan Milligan places the track against the rest of the record: “‘I’ll Be Your Hammer’ probably sounds more like our past releases than any other song on the album.” It follows the earlier single “The Wrong End of Your Rifle”, also featuring Connelly, which previewed “Apocalypse Pending” in April 2026. The 13-track album is available on digipack CD and digital. About The Joy Thieves The Joy Thieves are a Chicago industrial-rock collective led by Dan Milligan with James Scott, working through Joy Thieves Productions. The project builds tracks from fragments contributed by a large rotating roster of musicians drawn from the wider industrial and post-punk scene. The group signed to Armalyte Industries in 2018, and “Apocalypse Pending” is their eleventh release for the label. Chris Connelly is an Edinburgh-born singer and musician, a founding member of Fini Tribe who later worked with Ministry, Revolting Cocks and Pigface alongside a long solo catalogue. “I’ll Be Your Hammer” is the latest single lifted from “Apocalypse Pending”.
items._cn_summary: The Joy Thieves 与 Chris Connelly 合作的单曲《I'll Be Your Hammer》来自专辑《Apocalypse Pending》，由伦敦独立厂牌 Armalyte Industries 发行。这首歌的标题明显借鉴了 Velvet Underground 的《I'll Be Your Mirror》，但将其语义反转，从内省式的爱人之语转化为对抗威权压迫的抵抗宣言——歌词强调压制越多、力量越强。Dan Milligan 指出该曲延续了乐队以往作品的风格脉络。项目采用轮换乐手集体协作的模式，制作人横跨工业与后朋克场景。专辑共十三首曲目，已发行实体与数字版本。整体风格属于芝加哥工业摇滚传统，与用户关注的暗潮/工业/后朋克方向契合，但内容本质为新闻通稿，缺乏实际音乐分析与艺术价值评判。

items.body: Front 242, the Belgian electronic body music pioneers, now present their farewell live album “Black Out” on solid silver double vinyl as well, out on 25 September 2026 through Alfa Matrix. The new pressing follows the sold-out crystal clear and clear purple fanpack vinyl editions, and arrives alongside a Full Silver Pack bundle. Black Out (Deluxe Edition + 3 Hidden Bonus Tracks) by FRONT 242 What the ‘Black Out’ silver editions include Alfa Matrix pressed an additional 1,000 copies on solid silver vinyl after the earlier vinyl runs sold out ahead of the street date. The label states that demand was “nothing short of phenomenal”, with both the crystal clear transparent edition and the limited clear purple fanpack selling out before release. The solid silver 2LP carries 20 tracks across four sides and sells for 37,99 euro. The Full Silver Pack collects the solid silver 2LP together with the “Black Out” 2CD digipak, the Front 242 tribute “Recovery For You 2” on 2CD, and the label samplers “Sounds From The Matrix 26” and “Sounds From The Matrix 27”. Both editions are open for pre-order and street on 25 September 2026. Front 242, the ‘Black Out’ live album “Black Out” documents Front 242’s final tour, recorded at AB Brussels (Ancienne Belgique) in January 2025 during the band’s last hometown shows. Side-Line covered the album and its seven formats on its first release in June 2026. The set draws on a farewell run of more than 40 performances across six months in Europe and the USA, and includes the first official releases of three tracks the band had played live in recent years: “Generator”, “Fix It” and “Hide and Seek”. On stage for the recording, Patrick Codenys, Jean-Luc De Meyer and Richard 23 were joined by Tim Kroker on drums, with David Baboulis of SOLDOUT handling the studio mix and production. The double vinyl runs 20 tracks across four sides – “W.Y.H.I.W.Y.G.”, “Moldavia”, “Body to Body”, “Don’t Crash”, “Operating Tracks”, “U-Men”, “Funkhadafi”, “Quite Unusual”, “Generator”, “Commando Mix”, “Gripped by Fear”, “Take One”, “Red Team”, “Fix It”, “Punish your Machine”, “Tragedy for You”, “Hide and Seek”, “Welcome to Paradise”, “Happiness” and “HeadHunter”. The 2CD digipak extends the set to 23 tracks with three exclusives, “MasterHit”, “Soul Manager” and “No Shuffle”. The band paired the farewell with a short statement. “It is with a heavy mix of emotion that we close this great adventure, some 40 years in the making. We realize that ending our journey at this time, when we are still vibrant and full of energy is how the band should be remembered,” Front 242 said when they announced the final tour. About Front 242 Front 242 formed in 1981 in Belgium, founded by Daniel Bressanutti and Dirk Bergen. Patrick Codenys and Jean-Luc De Meyer soon joined, and Richard 23 completed the classic four-piece in 1982. The band were among the pioneers of electronic body music, and used the term as a self-description on the 1984 album “No Comment”. Across the following decades Front 242 released “Geography” (1982), “No Comment” (1984), “Official Version” (1987) and “Front by Front” (1988), the album that carried “Headhunter”, followed by “Tyranny (For You)” (1991), the paired “06:21:03:11 Up Evil” and “05:22:09:12 Off” (1993) and “Pulse” (2003). Daniel Bressanutti stepped back from touring in 2018, and the group played its final concerts at Front 242’s hometown venue AB Brussels in January 2025. “Black Out” documents those shows, and the solid silver 2LP and Full Silver Pack are its newest editions.
items._cn_summary: Front 242 这张告别现场专辑《Black Out》记录了乐队在布鲁塞尔 AB 剧院的终场演出，音源来自持续六个月的四十余场欧美巡演。专辑以双黑胶形式发行，收录二十首曲目横跨四面，另在双 CD 版本中追加三首独占曲目，包括曾在现场演出但从未正式发行的《Generator》《Fix It》《Hide and Seek》。制作部分由 Soldout 的 David Baboulis 负责混音，舞台阵容包含核心成员 Patrick Codenys、Jean-Luc De Meyer、Richard 23 及鼓手 Tim Kroker。这是一份道别式的现场记录，既作为向乐迷的终极礼物，也是比利时电子工业先驱四十年音乐旅程的句点。

items.body:
Produced by Neek and Jabu's Amos Childs (aka O$VMV$M), Manonmars' third album is syrupy suite of smoke-hazed recollections and free associated reflections set to decelerated, semi-rhythmic bumps, sluggish samples and cloudy drones. Sturdy biz FFO Ka, MIKE, King Vision Ultra or Coby Sey.

Manonmars' 2018 debut is one of those albums we still go back to periodically. It's that rare meeting of minds: a space for O$VMV$M to flex their production muscle and a scratchpad for London-based MC, painter and photographer Jack Martyn Richardson to sketch out his vision of England. And his experiences and impressions on 'Entertainment System' still feel chewable. "Goddess on my arm and both our phones got no service," he quips on 'Goddess'. "Acid is lysergic, psychedelic rock is Turkish." His rhymes aren't throwaway, they map out an underground that's very recognisable, shadowed by O$VMV$M's tuff, effective soundscapes - beats that reference trip-hop, ambient music, exotica and '70s movie soundtracks as much as they do US rap. On opener 'Flam3throw3r', Mars raps in double-time over shrill horns that blot out any trace of a beat; Neek and Childs sound as if they're relishing the negative space, adding chic sword swipes to a track that's got little else to do with the Wu Tang Clan. And even when a lumbering beat kicks in on 'Decathlon', flipping from downtempo to no-tempo in the final act, it sounds as if it's just there to assert O$VMV$M's commitment to slowness - Mars doesn't even seem to notice, rhyming casually but never losing his internal flow.

On 'Nasyua', his slurred expressions duck and weave around industrial whirrs and animalistic groans. "There was a time when I had flaws now I've adapted," he slurs. "I hit the zoot like Steve Zissou in 'The Life Aquatic' / then I dashed it, Christian Bale in a facemask on some Bat shit." Bristol mainstays Franco Franco and Dali de Saint Paul turn up to assist on 'Volcanic Shield', one of the album's most conventional bangers, led by O$VMV$M's skittering Surf Gang-like beats and morse code blips, and cold light's Birthmark lends his voice to 'Infinite', going bar for bar with Mars over Neek and Childs' soupy slackened funk. These moments are when 'Entertainment System' really shines, blaring out like an old tape on a busted in-car audio system. 'Firewater' takes the same approach, leaving Mars to do his best as snares are reformed into splashes alongside sultry stabs and sax from Brum-based sound artist Lorenzo Prati. "My bitch white, she can scuba dive and ice climb," he spits. "Put the drink down, I wasn't in my right mind." It's music that laughs through the tears - what could be more British than that?
items._genre: abstract hip-hop / experimental hip-hop / electronic / ambient rap
items._cn_summary: 这是Manonmars的第三张专辑，由制作人组合O$VMV$M操刀。整张作品以一种黏稠、烟雾缭绕的质感铺陈开来，减速的半律动节拍、迟缓的采样与浑浊的低鸣构成松散的声场底色。伦敦MC Jack Martyn Richardson的押韵并非随意堆砌，而是勾勒出一幅可辨认的英国地下图景。制作上融合了trip-hop、ambient、exotica及七十年代电影配乐的语汇，歌词在双倍速与漫不经心之间切换。客串阵容包括Bristol的Franco Franco、Dali de Saint Paul以及Cold Light的Birthmark，客座乐手Lorenzo Prati贡献了萨克斯线条。专辑在'Volcanic Shield'与'Firewater'等曲目中呈现出相对传统的硬核节奏形态，但整体更强调负空间与慢速美学，试图在嘻哈骨架下构建一种沉浸式、近乎环境音乐的听感。

items.body:
Kelela's third album isn't quite the indie rock pivot that we all expected but it's a breath of fresh air all the same, trading d-club and nu-ambient wooze for low-lit Prince-style funk, hypnagogic 2-step and sensual minimal R&B. Genuinely sexy, joyful gear FFO Dijon, Jai Paul, Dawuna and PinkPantheress.

It was tough to know exactly what to think when Kelela dropped the shoegaze-y 'idea 1' in April, citing her tenure on the D.C. indie scene as her third album's core motivation. Were we about to get a Kelela rock album? Well, not exactly. As the name suggests, 'new avatar' is a reboot of sorts that breaks confidently away from the whirr of modish snaps and hum of gliding squares that powered records as iconic as 'Cut 4 Me' and 'Hallucinogen', even lapping at the edges of 2023's 'Raven'. Skeletal and unashamedly erotic, it's still a Kelela record, but one that's been stripped back to the bare bones, dreamed up almost entirely by Kelela herself, alongside just two co-producers: PinkPantheress collaborator Oscar Scheller and A.K. Paul. The best indication we have for the general tone of this one is actually 'In the Blue Light', last year's powerful live album that reimagined a selection of her classic tracks for a two-night appearance at New York City's Blue Note Jazz Club. That set was a victory lap for Kelela, who'd begun her career as a jazz singer when she was at college, and she completes her flashback here, fast-forwarding to her time as the lead vocalist in indie outfit Dizzy Spells.

'idea 1' opens the record and contextualises it immediately, forgoing the expected beat and prioritizing distorted guitar textures and jazzy harmonics. Just like it did on 'In the Blue Light', Kelela's voice has the space it needs to really stand out, growing from a whisper into a saturated cry during the dense chorus. So even through 'point blank' finds her on more familiar turf, cooing over floury amen chops, TX81z "Lately bass" stings and downsampled FM stabs, we hear it with different ears. Because 'point blank' is the outlier here; by the time we reach 'goin down', Kelela is decrying failed relationships over filtered Linn drums and glitch'd waves of chorus-kinked guitar that wouldn't be out of place on an mk.gee record. And all of this makes 'outta time', her goosebump-inducing Prince-esque collaboration with A.K. Paul, hit that much harder, with Paul's gentle, intuitive touches just adding deeper relevance to the 'new avatar' as it unfolds. It prepares us for 'crystallize', an immediately entry into the Kelela songbook that's a bridge between her different eras, beginning like a track from 'Cut 4 U' before exploding into a 'Sign O' The Times'-style power ballad.

So the album's relatively more animated final stretch actually comes as a surprise, beginning with the Craig David-sampling 'don't piss me off', a wormish 2-step memory that follows in the mould of 'Untrue' and hitting a high point with 'The Bridge', another syncopated slow burner that fittingly features PinkPantheress. These tracks are a wink to listeners who've been holding out since the early days as Kelela embraces the future. It would have been disingenuous to present an album that imagines everything's fine, so Kelela looks for the joy in the everyday - the memories we thought we'd lost, even the failed relationships - and arrives on her most spirited and assertive full-length yet.
items._cn_summary: 这是Kelela的第三张专辑，从此前标志性的去俱乐部化和新氛围电子风格中抽身，转向更内省的方向。整张作品由她本人主导创作，仅与两位制作人合作——Oscar Scheller和A.K. Paul。开场曲'idea 1'以失真吉他纹理和爵士和声取代了惯用节拍，为整张专辑定下基调。'outta time'是与A.K. Paul合作的Prince式放克曲目，层次丰富；'crystallize'则是连接不同创作时期的桥梁作品。专辑后半段相对更具活力，'don't piss me off'采样了Craig David，呈现出2-step舞曲质感。'In the Blue Light'现场专辑中展现的爵士根源和作为Dizzy Spells主唱的独立乐队经历在此得到延伸和融合。整体而言，作品剥离了繁复制作，回归人声本身，将放克、R&B、2-step和独立摇滚元素编织成一张私密而性感的专辑。

items.body:
The key members of Animal Collective & Spacemen 3 yield a sumptuous 2nd duo LP of ‘60s Beach Boys harmonies via garage-psych-dub-pop and tied off with a ribbon-bow of lysergic studio sorcery, everything soft and glowing to the touch. Happy days...

"It is built on loops of harp (Mary Lattimore) and sequences of steel drum, webs of pedal steel and even bits of a mariachi band. These are, of course, deliberate choices, sounds and textures they’ve never used and that offered a clear sonic break from the success of Reset. But maybe more than ever, Sonic Boom and Panda Bear emerge through these 10 songs as two people with frank opinions about these times, with a real stake in the sway of the world. These tunes grapple with online exhaustion and pervasive depression, with political chicanery and ecological sustainability, all while advocating for respecting the power of luck and giving one another grace in a moment when very few of us actually know what the hell is happening.

Has it ever been easier to complain publicly about something without trying to change it? Sonic Boom and Panda Bear are not content to gripe about circumstances or speculate about the fall on A ? of WHEN. The goal is for the music to create physical connections between people, to encourage them to enjoy a real experience in the world with it and each other."

items.body:
Bit of a special one from John T. Gast’s 5 Gate Temple, finding anomalous wildcard St Agnis with a set of classical guitar improvisations under the Victoria Mingot alias - all enchantingly loose-limbed lowercase strums and murmurs tipped for fans of Loren Connors, Graham Lambkin, Virginia Astley, Vincent Gallo, Klein.

‘God Spill’ runs like a diary of broken sleep, taking things to their quietest, most ruminative depths. The dozen pieces are defined by plaintive melodic structuring for classical guitar, voice and pedals, on what sounds like dictaphone recordings that imbue everything with an eerie ferric intimacy. And those vocals are pretty special when they do appear, like a flickering filament in the aether of ‘i saw the sign’, recalling Mary Maddox off Mike Ratledge’s ‘Riddles of the Sphinx’, floating, Virginia Astley-like, on the frayed Lambkin-esque strum of ‘in plentitude of the harvest’, or more textural in the mournful raga meditation ‘om dhyana’.

The exquisitely discreet balance of un-showy yet transfixing instrumental economy is magnified by an un-moored sense of time and place and what the label call “soft rage” -  fully revealing itself with repeat listens.

Special stuff.
items._genre: experimental / lowercase / improvised classical guitar / ambient folk
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了十二首以古典吉他为核心的低保真即兴录音，辅以人声、效果器与盒式磁带录音质感，营造出安静、沉思的氛围。人声在吉他拨弦间若隐若现，呈现出飘渺、近乎气音的质感，与破碎的旋律结构形成呼应。整张作品带有强烈的私密日记感，时间与空间感模糊，介于梦呓与冥想之间。曲目中可见印度音乐元素的影响（如'om dhyana'），呈现出拉格式冥想的质地。制作上强调低调内敛，演奏经济克制，在反复聆听中逐渐显露深度。该专辑来自 John T. Gast 创立的地下厂牌5 Gate Temple，独立小众发行，与当代古典、实验即兴等领域有交集，但在融合深度上仍有较大空间。

items.body:
25 year re-up for Aubrey Hoermann’s cult slab of gritty 313 electro-techno minimalism on Mono Horizon, the US label behind that ace Trevor Dale reissue.

‘The Dance Flo-Funk EP’ was originally cooked up by Hoermann as the 4th in a handful of 12”s on his Odic Force label, which ran between 1998-2002. It’s straight-up Detroit dancefloor sex that has led to its cult status by collectors and DJs seeking the special spice for durational sessions, hitting where it matters between the brittle, ascetic budge of ‘Dff’, the unadulterated raw baseline sleaze of ‘Woodblockpop’, a squirming tracky jack tool ‘Df’, and the tendon-tuning fidget of ‘Corecharge’.

Damn effective, damn obscure, tackle from tha D!
items._cn_summary: 这张EP是Aubrey Hoermann于2000年前后在底特律创作的电子舞曲作品，由独立厂牌Mono Horizon进行25周年再版发行。整张唱片聚焦于极简主义的电声律动，四首曲目各自呈现不同的质感与功能性：脆硬克制的'Dff'展现极简美学，粗粝低频主导的'Woodblockpop'强调原始感官冲击，'Df'作为轨道化的DJ工具提供持续的节奏驱动力，而'Corecharge'则以紧绷的律动细节著称。整张作品专为长时段DJ场景设计，融合底特律电子舞曲的冷峻与功能性，具有较高的收藏价值。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — The brainchild of classically trained guitarist Jan Zehrfeld, PANZERBALLETT which is a German termreferring to a military tank ballet emerged in Munich in 2005 with its energetic and innovativebrand of jazz metal that is as equally regarded for its emotional connecting humor and funk-fueledsong structures as it is for unleashing a blitzkrieg of technical workouts. This band is legendaryin the live circuit and to the modern day has released eight well-regarded albums which all beganwith this self-titled one from 2006, the year after the band's inception. While the rather limitedworld of jazz metal usually results in a metal band such as Atheist or Cynic coming from the metalworld and incorporating jazz chords and styles into its mix, PANZERBALLETT has been much moiregrounded on the jazz side of the equation with a virtuosic saxophone being delivered by Alexandervon Hagke along with its Messhugah inspired djent-metal approach. Despite being an exclusively instrumental band that was inspired by not only the intricate jazzdisplays of The Weather Report, Tribal Tech and Herbie Hancock but also the avant-prog workouts ofacts such as Mats Morgan and the wily math metal antics of Meshuggah and similarly minded metal.While the band would eventually incorporate prominent technically infused covers of pop acts such asABBA and others like Frank Zappa and even theme songs from TV shows such as The Simpsons, on thiseponymous debut PANZERBALLETT sticks to its own original compositions that feature less of thecreative whimsy that would highlight them amongst the world of progressive jazz fusion metal. Thisalbum is more of a no nonsense declaration that a new band is in town and this ain't your parents'jazz fusion any longer which in 2006 was still somewhat of a novelty in the world of metal (andfrankly still is!)Noticeably less metallic than its future releases, album #1 focuses more on a staccato driven jazzmetal effect that offers intricately complex compositions exuding jazz flavors and melodic workoutswhile adding the heft of guitar grunge to offer the contrast. While the guitar soloing is in actionhere, it's not to the level that Zerfeld would unleash on future releases. The opening "Zerfunk"pretty much sets the stage with a funky bass groove that finds labyrinthine jazz explorations lacedwith guitar chord prominence and occasional soloing prowess however in the end the album soundsfairly uniform and lacks that wild explorative energy that the band would become famous for both inthe studio and in a live setting. This album features nine well constructed tracks but lacks thecreative mojo that would soon take root beginning with the band's second release which would debutthe whacky jazz metal interpretations of totally diverse cover songs only in instrumental form.Overall not a bad debut as PANZERBALLETT definitely delivers a unique take on the world of jazzmetal that focuses first and foremost on the jazz aspects with a prominent saxophone presence andkeeping the metallic furor at bay. While the metal would become a stronger playing card on futurerelease and the two styles would become more integrated, this self-titled debut is by no means awasted effort as it generates a wild and exhilarating ride through metal-tinged jazz-funk-fusionwith blistering technical workouts decorated with intimate softer jazz oriented passages, a traitwhich would only diversify on future releases. A great beginning if not the band's primo offering.This album is bogged down by the tracks being too similar and not enough creative mojo had yet beenmustered up to make a completely compelling album as one would experience on the electrifying albumssuch as "Hart Genossen von Abba bis Zappa." Still though this album really rocks the jazz unlike anyother.3.5 rounded down
items._genre: jazz metal / jazz fusion / progressive rock / instrumental
items._cn_summary: 这张2005年问世的同名首作由德国慕尼黑乐队PANZERBALLETT创作，核心人物是古典出身的吉他手Jan Zehrfeld。乐队将爵士乐置于主导地位，以Alexander von Hagke的萨克斯独奏为核心，同时融入Meshuggah式的djent金属节奏质感，形成爵士与金属的跨界碰撞。作品全为器乐演奏，灵感源自Weather Report、Tribal Tech、Herbie Hancock等爵士名家，亦受Mats Morgan等前卫团体影响。九首原创曲目以断奏式的爵士金属织体构建，融合funk律动、复杂爵士和声与吉他grunge质感。与乐队后续以流行翻唱和荒诞创意著称的专辑相比，这张首作风格更为直接纯粹，重在宣示新乐队对传统爵士融合的颠覆。整体展现技术扎实但创意锋芒尚处萌芽阶段的探索姿态。

items.body: Just look away From her cold smile I walk away from The one I admire Border Goth trio The Slashes stare into the flames with their latest single, I Started A Fire, a song that carries the charge of a band stepping into the room with the lights dimmed yet every nerve twitching awake. From the first seconds, melodic guitars carve out its bleak horizon, while the bass pushes forward with purpose and Esteban Rene’s deep vocals pull the song into a place where desire feels dangerous because it knows exactly what it wants. The San Diego trio has always drawn from more than one map. The Slashes are shaped by the crosscurrents of border-town air, cold-wave chill, rock en español romance, and the kind of nocturnal rock music that seems to find you when the rest of the city has gone quiet. On I Started A Fire, that blend feels especially sharp. Beto Bautista’s bass gives the track its engine, Carlos Robles keeps the drums upbeat and restless, and the production folds in synth and cello touches that widen the frame without softening the bite. I Started A Fire follows the collapse into destructive infatuation. The beloved remains emotionally distant, yet the speaker keeps moving closer, surrendering to obsession as both trap and purpose. Love becomes a self-inflicted wound, sparked by the singer’s own hand, until escape begins to lose its appeal. By the end, devotion has taken on the shape of an eclipse: permanent, darkly romantic, and strangely peaceful in its damage. The rhythm keeps pressing ahead, but the atmosphere around it carries a wound. The guitars have a clean, melodic sting, never overplaying their hand, while the low end gives the track its strut through the darkened streets. Esteban Rene sings like someone who has learned that romance and ruin can walk through the same door. His delivery never sounds detached from the drama. He sounds caught inside it, watching the flames rise and deciding, perhaps too late, that the fire is part of the attraction. That is the strange charm of The Slashes. They make music for the restless, for the doomed romantics, for the people who discover a band at 2 a.m. and wake up still thinking about them. “I Started A Fire” is sleek, dramatic, and alive with border-goth voltage, a song that turns the ache of wanting someone harmful into something you can dance through before the smoke catches up. Listen to I STARTED A FIRE below and order the single here. I STARTED A FIRE by The Slashes The Slashes play Soda Bar in San Diego on July 28th. Follow The Slashes: Instagram Facebook Bandcamp The post “Our Eclipse is Here” — Border Goth Trio the Slashes Stare into the Flames With “I Started A Fire” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items._cn_summary: Evanescence第六张专辑邀来Jordan Fish等三位制作人合作，在保留原有厚重感的基础上引入哥特与工业摇滚元素。整张作品的编曲以Amy Lee的美声为核心向外辐射，忧伤的旋律与阴郁的质感交织。开场曲"Afterlife"以忧郁而明亮的旋律成为亮点，专辑整体追求跨越年龄层的普遍共鸣。制作阵容的多元为声音带来了新的层次，但整体仍处于主流摇滚的可预期框架内，哥特与工业元素的融合更多体现在氛围营造而非结构突破上。作为一支成熟的乐队，他们在延续辨识度的同时尝试拓展声音边界，这种探索值得肯定但尚未达到彻底革新的程度。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)
items.label: Bongo Joe
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录圣多美和普林西比1970至80年代的声音，风格被称为Puxa，融合了前葡萄牙非洲殖民地音乐元素，包括merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等。岛屿面积小、音乐场景有限，却诞生了多把吉他交织缠绕、即兴呼应的复杂器乐结构，节奏层丰富、贝斯与键盘时常退场让鼓与吉他主导律动。Pedro Lima领衔的乐队展示了与鼓手对位、旁注式吉他评论的编制，Sangazuza展示了鼓与吉他驱动的疯克律动。Africa Negra等团体的作品以呼应式人声融入旋律框架，展开可延伸至数小时的现场即兴段落。整体展现了非洲小岛殖民遗产与跨大西洋音乐交流交织的独特面貌。

items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这张马里音乐专辑由巴拉风琴演奏者内巴·索洛与恩贡尼演奏者贝内戈·迪亚基特合作完成，原始录音于2013年在巴马科由乌斯曼·哈伊达拉完成，后经制片人尼克·戈尔德与英国音乐人桑尼·约翰斯重新编排为合奏作品，加入弦乐、麦尔特龙、吉他与打击乐层叠，并以索洛及三位女歌手的和声叠加。专辑以双CD形式呈现，前半部分为重塑的合奏版本，后半部分保留原始二重奏录音。曲目以恩贡尼的反复riff为结构基础，索洛在巴拉风琴上即兴并主唱，弦乐点缀克制而不喧宾夺主。迪亚基特与索洛来自不同音乐背景，这种罕见的两件马里传统乐器组合经过细致再制作，保留了曼丁音乐典型的呼应式演唱特质，同时拓展了原声音响的层次感。

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?

items._cn_summary: Canzoniere Grecanico Salentino以这张专辑纪念乐队五十年历程，核心策略是由新一代成员重新演绎父辈Rina与Daniele Durante时期的曲目，保留pizzica的原始能量与地域根源，同时加入合成器贝斯等电声元素扩展声响色彩。专辑收录与钢琴家Einaudi合作的Taranta项目混音版，并邀请家族成员如Roberto Licci与Emanuele父子、早期主唱Rossella Pinto共同演唱，形成跨代际对话。整体仍以原声乐器为主，pizzica的干燥律动贯穿全作，既是对传统的致敬，也是对这门源自南意大利的音乐如何走向全球舞台的一次梳理。

items.excerpt: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music.
items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. Further listening: Duo Ruut - Ilmateade Maria Moramarco, Fabio Mina, and Francesco Savoretti - Pietrafonie Jaune Toujours - Vertigo

items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku暌违多年的第四张专辑，将北欧民间旋律与巴尔干音乐语汇相互融合。专辑围绕保加利亚民间舞蹈节奏、马其顿情歌等素材展开创作，旋律感敏锐，作品兼具明快的舞曲气息与内省的忧郁气质。末曲为纪念已故母亲七十岁生日而作，从沉静的挽歌式铺陈逐渐转向超脱的吟唱，真挚而深沉。整体呈现一位北欧音乐人对东南欧传统的真诚呼应，跨界意识清晰，但手法偏向传统民谣范畴内的融合，实验性与声音设计层面较为克制。

items.body: W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes This collaboration between the five-piece Belgian instrumental group W�r, whose members specialize in bringing the music of earlier centuries to life, and Kongero, the acclaimed Swedish female acapella folk quartet, offers an unusual chance to explore how their two cultures, ostensibly so different, can come together. It might sounds an unlikely mix, but here�s a spoiler: it turns out they�re pretty much musical best friends. The album kicks off at a cracking pace with �Var �r Du?�, a bravura performance through a twisted, tortuous piece that manages to be both elegant and surprising. However, the true astonishment arrives at the end, when the audience applauds and you suddenly realize this was recorded live (actually over two separate performances). W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes The musicians bring material from their separate traditions, plus one original, showcasing their skills in intricate, swinging arrangements for both instruments and voices. Thanks to their skill, the varied ideas fit together seamlessly so it�s brimming with delights, like the wonderfully-titled �Drinking Like A Sweet Swede,� where the singers layers their harmonies over a jaunty backing. Everything is intricate, performed with a glowing precision that can disarm the senses with its beauty. The highlight, perhaps, is the beautiful �Klosterjungfrun.� The slow, seductive opening draws in the listener, the voices airy and light, curling around each other as the instruments wind long their path their. It�s a beautiful piece, but really, just one gem among so many here. W�R, Kongero - Songbooks Live by Nordic Notes There�s never a foot wrong, no note out of place and the performances are passionate, stellar, a true collaboration of instruments and voices. Add to that a mix that�s sharp as a razor, and Songbooks Live is a truly outstanding album, a perfect illustration that people have more in common than separates them. And it illustrates exactly what artists can achieve live. With luck, they�ll work together again. Soon, please. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由比利时器乐组合Wûr与瑞典阿卡贝拉女声四重唱Kongero合作完成，双方分别带来各自传统中的曲目，并融入一首原创作品。Wûr专注于演绎数世纪前的欧洲音乐，Kongero则以北欧民谣无伴奏合唱著称，专辑录制于两场现场演出，展现了乐器与人声在复杂编排中的交织。编曲注重对位与和声层次，人声轻盈环绕，器乐则提供行进式支撑，整体呈现出文艺复兴与巴洛克风格的精致感。混音清晰锐利，突出现场表演的活力与互动。这种比利时与瑞典两种文化的交汇虽然素材传统，但通过跨地域合作呈现出音乐共性的探索，是一次兼具学术性与可听性的世界音乐尝试。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇来自Bandcamp Daily的当代古典音乐月度推荐汇编，聚焦于作曲驱动型作品。文章简要介绍了当代古典音乐在分类上的复杂性，涵盖电子实验、即兴演奏以及对经典作品的大胆重新诠释等内容。作为一篇月度榜单导言，文章本身并非针对具体专辑的深度乐评，而是对选辑范围和标准的概述性说明。文中提及的音乐风格与用户关注的当代古典、实验音乐及电子方向高度契合，但因内容为导言性质，缺乏对具体作品细节、创作手法或艺术价值的深入分析，信息量有限。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — BEAT is a supergroup that was put together in 2024 by Adrian Belew and Tony Levin with the aim ofreinterpreting and playing live the material from King Crimson's monumental triptych of studioalbums released in the 1980s. Joining this all-American tribute act are guitarist Steve Vai and Tooldrummer Danny Carey, arguably forming one of the most stellar tribute lineups ever. The projectwould, of course, receive the blessings of both Robert Fripp and Bill Bruford, allowing the newly-formed touring project to begin working on their live interpretations of some of the most innovativeand iconic music from the 80s. All of this led to a very intriguing 2025 release on Inside Out Music- 'Neon Heat Disease: Live in Los Angeles', which is the official live album documenting thequartet's 2024-25 US tour.Essentially featuring two sets and a two-song encore (that is generally attributed to the secondset), this album features live covers of the majority of the King Crimson songs appearing acrosstheir 'Discipline', 'Beat', and 'Three of a Perfect Pair' albums. The energy is infectious and theperformances of all four band members are immaculate, as one could imagine. Most songs are playedfaithfully to the originals, although there are several moments where the experimental side of thelineup takes over, especially on the prolonged renditions of 'Industry' and 'The Sheltering Sky'(respectively ten and fourteen minutes long). Adrian Belew's voice sound incredible some forty yearson, and his guitar experiments definitely bring a wilder edge to the show and the live recordings,while Tony Levin switches between his iconic Chapman stick and his classic bass guitar. Steve Vai'srole is incredibly important here, as he approaches Fripp's monumental parts quite respectfully,even if he allows himself a few ripping solos here and there. Danny Carey's performances areimmensely impressive as well, as he nails down some of the most sophisticated prog rhythms of alltime.The setlist on the CD release is essentially what BEAT play every other night, so this release giveslisteners an excellent chance to experience the vibrant mastery of this tribute band. Furthermore,each track is a highlight on is own, and despite a few rough parts (eventually owed to the recordingand the subsequent mixing), both the disc and the actual live shows are a spectacular treat for KingCrimson afficionados! This album also marks (very likely) the first ever live renditions of 'ModelMan', 'Dig Me', and 'Man with an Open Heart' from 1984's 'Three of a Perfect Pair', which is prettyinteresting in itself alone.
items._genre: progressive rock / art rock / experimental rock
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑由Adrian Belew与Tony Levin于2024年组建的超级团体BEAT录制，吉他手Steve Vai与Tool鼓手Danny Carey共同参与，演绎King Crimson八十年代三张开创性录音室专辑《Discipline》《Beat》《Three of a Perfect Pair》中的作品。专辑包含两段主歌单加两首返场曲，多数曲目忠于原版，但工业与庇护天空等曲目的现场延伸版展现出乐手们的实验倾向。Belew的嗓音与吉他实验、Levin在Chapman Stick与贝斯间的切换、Vai对Fripp原声部的诠释以及Carey对复杂节奏的把握均被详细讨论。专辑也首次呈现了《Model Man》《Dig Me》《Man with an Open Heart》等曲目的现场版本。评论整体正面，但内容属于对tribute性质的演出记录，原创性有限。

items.body: Review by antonyus — When I first listened to At the End of the Day, I wasn't completely convinced. I enjoyed the atmosphere, but I felt the songs were a little too restrained compared to Nemrud's previous albums. Nothing jumped out at me immediately.A few more listens changed everything.This is the kind of album that doesn't try to impress you with technical fireworks or constant twists. Instead, it slowly reveals its depth through its melodies, carefully layered keyboards, and subtle instrumental details. Every time I came back to it, I noticed something new a guitar phrase hiding beneath the keyboards, a Mellotron line adding warmth, or a bass melody quietly holding everything together.What I appreciate most is how confidently Nemrud have embraced their own identity. The classic progressive rock influences are still there, but they never feel like a tribute act. The Hammond organ, Mellotron, and vintage synth sounds create a familiar atmosphere, yet the songwriting feels fresh and personal. The heavier moments have real weight, while the softer passages never lose their emotional impact.My favourite moment on the album is probably "Return to Void," although picking a single track almost feels unfair. At the End of the Day is a true concept album, where each piece naturally leads into the next. Rather than standing on their own, the songs feel like chapters of the same story, making the album far more rewarding when heard from beginning to end. Return to Void perfectly captures that feeling with its hypnotic atmosphere, subtle Eastern influences, and patient build-up. It's one of those pieces that doesn't demand your attention it quietly earns it, and before you realize it, you're already moving toward the album's emotional finale.At the End of the Day isn't an album that gives away all its secrets on the first listen. It slowly draws you into its world, and once you're there, it's difficult to stop before the final notes of The Gate. That's probably its greatest strength it never feels like a collection of songs, but a single musical journey. With every listen, the details become clearer, and the emotional impact grows stronger. For me, this is Nemrud's most complete and rewarding album to date.Final Rating: 4.5/5

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由Nemrud乐队于2025年发行的迷幻/太空摇滚专辑，被定位为概念专辑形式。乐评者描述起初对作品持保留态度，认为歌曲较为克制，但经过多次聆听后逐渐发现其层次深度。专辑的核心特质在于不依赖炫技或频繁转折，而是通过旋律、键盘层次、合成器音色以及Mellotron、Hammond风琴等复古元素来逐步展现细节。乐评特别提及东欧音乐人身份带来的东方音乐元素融入，体现在'Return to Void'一曲的氛围营造中。整体评价强调专辑作为完整音乐旅程的概念连贯性，从开篇到终曲'The Gate'形成统一的叙事弧线，被认为是乐队迄今为止最完整且情感回报最高的作品。

items.body: Review by alainPP — 1. "Divided by One" for reviving that "resistance" message; otherwise, the tune is monolithic?more tinkered-with than creative?flirting painfully with an 80s sound and adding nothing new.2. "Chaos Dreaming" for its slow, synth-driven drift; the hang drum and Japanese-style guitar bring a breath of fresh air to a disembodied, sketchy melody that takes a long time to take shape?though the track itself lacks soul and rhythm.3. "Sirensong," which reinforces a haunting, persistent mood with distant cries; the finale finds energy in a repetitive melody reminiscent of "The Lamb Lies Down on Broadway" (the "Archangel" era)?a definite plus.4. "Pool of Mirrors," featuring distant Asian influences and whispered vocals?somewhere between New Age and Tangerine Dream's cinematic tracks; its soporific length and languor make one want to skip past it?a recurring issue with the album.5. "Heaven's Rain" finally reassures me, offering a touch of gentleness and solemnity through the flute, delicate synth pads, and the concluding thunderstorm.6. "Screaming Sound Machines" falls back into the habit of eclectic synths that merely plink out notes rather than projecting them; a Collins-esque vocal?paired with a beautiful guitar solo by Steve?holds the attention; the real highlight is the 10-second finale, though it remains underdeveloped.7. "Heavy Water," marking a return to a Japanese-style cinematic ambient sound; it evokes a track from the Gabriel era?in both lead and backing vocals?and is undoubtedly the best song, thanks to its cinematic scope and Roland Buhlmann's plaintive guitar work.8. "Inviolate Fields," redolent of Mike Oldfield's bell-infused atmospheres, featuring vocals by Laura (known for her work with Clive Nolan). A simple, atmospheric tune with ethereal backing vocals creating a serene mood and a magnificent, Popol Vuh-esque outro?though, again, too short.9. "Are Friends Electric?"?capturing Gary Numan's signature velvety keyboard sound and vocals reminiscent of the "Archangel" era. Too monolithic for those sounds typical of a bygone era. The developments unfold at a snail's pace?far too long. Suitable for elevator music.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以键盘为主导铺陈氛围，融合新世纪的冥想气质与电影配乐式的场景感。乐评指其大量曲目在合成器驱动下过于冗长单调，旋律松散且缺乏内在节奏。作品中可辨识出加里·努曼式的键盘音色、东瀛风格的吉他点缀以及人声氛围，个别段落以长笛、柔弱合成器垫音和雷声结尾展现出温柔庄严的气质，被认为是专辑中最有说服力的部分。整体听感被比作升降机音乐，发展推进迟缓，情感内核较为稀薄。尽管有罗兰·布曼的吉他独奏与波波尔·维风格尾奏等亮点，但多数曲目因长度失控和创意不足而流于堆砌，是一张偏向氛围而非真正具有前卫实验精神的跨界前卫摇滚作品。

items.body: Review by TheEliteExtremophile — Witch Ripper is one of my favorite local acts, and they're always near the top of my list of bandsto recommend. Through the Hourglass is this quartet's third full-length release, and it is a directsequel to their last release, 2023's The Flight after the Fall. The shared story of these records isobvious, even without looking at the lyrics, with the music here bearing clear throughlines fromTFATF.My first exposure to this record was at Witch Ripper's album release show earlier this month. Theyplayed it in its entirety, and it was a killer performance. On subsequent listens, the album hasgrown on me even more.After the brief intro "Odyssey in Retrograde", which revisits some musical themes from their lastalbum, "The Portal" storms forth with melodic sludge metal. Witch Ripper's signature mixture ofclean and harsh vocals lends some great textural variation while a steady rhythm drives this pieceforward. The atmosphere is rich and enveloping, and there's a strong sense of forward momentum. Theband does a great job of evoking the feeling of traveling through the titular portal. The song'ssecond half also features some fantastic and fun soloing."Symmetry of the Hourglass" opens with bass-heavy, thumping sludge, but the drumming is deft andnimble, giving this a very kinetic feel. Guitar lines spiral and interlock in tense patterns onemoment and open up into broad, spacy arpeggios the next. As this cut evolves, classic proginfluences come to the fore with astral guitar lines, subtle synth embellishments, and soaringvocals."Echoes and Dust" is another energetic cut, with a constant upward push in intensity. This featuressome of the heaviest riffs on the record, and some exotic scales are deployed to add some greatvariance to the overall sound. There's more fantastic soloing as this song reaches its climax, andthere are flashes of acts like Coheed & Cambria and early Muse where Witch Ripper blends theirsludge roots with artsy alt-rock.Rippling, watery clean guitar opens "The Clock Queen" on a contemplative note. More subtle touchesof synth appear here, and I really appreciate the fullness that adds to the sound, as well as theirrestraint with those textures. Stuttering, nervous riffs give the verses an anxious feel, and I lovethe way palm-muted clean guitar is used to similar effect as pizzicato violin to evoke close andtense atmospheres in orchestral pieces and film scores. Hints of Dream Theater are here, too,especially in certain guitar melodies. The climax is especially grand and majestic."Proxima Centauri" is the gentlest song in Witch Ripper's whole catalog, at least in its first half.The tempo is sedate, drumming is light and diffuse, and the vocals are delicately sung. It's a nicebreather after such an intense set of songs prior to this. The guitar work is intricate and artful,and eschewing distortion really allowed the guitarists to show off their chops with minimaldistractions. Even once the distortion comes in, the focus is on big, melodic guitar lines and someclassically-influenced composition and playing.Through the Hourglass closes on its longest song, "The Spiral Eye". The riffs are looming and doom-laden, and the sound of a bell tolling only adds to that sense of dread. Guitars twist andintertwine, coiling around one another. Around this song's midpoint, this maelstrom dissolves into atense passage of clean guitar, hand percussion, and wordless vocals. Those wordless vocals continueeven after the full band rejoins, adding great weight and a sense of eerie foreboding.Witch Ripper's new album is another fantastic outing from this band. The flow of the record issmooth and makes sense, and nothing feels out of place. While it lacks the obvious crowning opusthat closes out their last album, the overall quality here is stellar. The band has taken up themantle of bands like Mastodon and Baroness in their brand of complex, progressive sludge.Originally published here: theeliteextremophile.com/2026/04/27/album-review-witch-ripper-through-the-hourglass/

items._cn_summary: 这是Witch Ripper乐队的第三张全长专辑，作为2023年《The Flight after the Fall》的直接续篇延续了共同的叙事主题。专辑将浊流金属的厚重质感与前卫摇滚的结构思维相融合，开场曲《The Portal》以旋律化的浊流铺陈，配合干净人声与嘶吼的交替形成丰富的层次变化。《Symmetry of the Hourglass》在贝斯主导的律动中展现了吉他线条的张弛转换，融入太空摇滚式的合成器点缀。《The Clock Queen》运用拨片闷音的清音吉他模拟小提琴拨奏的紧张感，兼具Dream Theater式旋律审美。器乐编排注重氛围构建与动态推进，每首曲目在曲式发展中包含独奏段落与情绪高潮，整体制作兼顾了浊流金属的重量感与前卫摇滚的复杂性。作为乐队所在地西雅图的本地乐队，作品带有美国地下金属场景的气质。
